Hi Folks,

I recently learned that there is a flexible tool called gtable that make ggplot2 capable of doing almost everything. It actually helped me in one of my recent project.

I would like to know more about gtable. Do you guys know any good doc/tutorial? Reading the CRAN manual is just too hard for me.

Thank you very much.

Best Regards,
Yue Zhao

messages.author: a3c668b849637905
messages.subject: Re: Abridged summary of ggplot2@googlegroups.com - 7 Messages in 5 Topics
parts:
Hi,

I don't think there is much of a reference, it's still under development (though it has been on halt for a year). I've started a wiki page, mainly as a collection of links to relevant SO questions,

https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/wiki/gtable

Feel free to add things and turn it into a useful reference. I'm happy to help (if I can), but I don't have the time to write a comprehensive tutorial.

The best way to learn, I think, is to play with it and browse the list of functions. They all have pretty self-describing names. There's a fairly long list of feature requests and other issues reported on its github development page, it's also a good place to learn more about the design.

baptiste

Actually, I find manual editing of wiki pages a bit frustrating and error-prone, so I've decided to fork gtable (Paul Murrell's fork) and work on a reproducible wiki page from there:

https://github.com/baptiste/gtable/blob/master/inst/wiki/gtable-intro.rmd

Running this page through knitr produces the output shown here,

https://github.com/baptiste/gtable/wiki/gtable-intro

Feel free to submit changes and additions.

Cheers,

baptiste
